questions.prompt: Choose one successful one-charge design from Challenge 1 or Challenge 2. State the source-charge sign and its position relative to the positive test charge. Explain how the local electric-field direction produced the force and changed the test charge's velocity.
questions.rubricText:
@[Always] Grading feedback: Evidence must describe a successful recorded Challenge 1 or Challenge 2 run. BusyBee scoring: Award points only in 0.5-point increments, including whole points, from 0 to the question maximum. Select a rubric-supported allowed score; never report hundredths such as 2.85/3. Do not average or percentage-scale rubric criteria into an off-grid score. A binary completion rubric still permits only 0 or full credit. Allowed scores for this question: 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2.
a. Full credit: Identifies the source sign and relative placement and correctly links field direction to force, acceleration, and the resulting velocity change. Partial credit: Gives a successful setup and correct attraction or repulsion but has an incomplete field-force-motion chain. No credit: Reverses the interaction or gives no usable run evidence.

questions.prompt: Write a claim-evidence-reasoning conclusion explaining how your successful Challenge 3 source-charge arrangement guided the positive test charge around the barrier. Cite the signs and locations of your charges and explain vector addition, net force, acceleration, and the changing velocity direction.
questions.rubricText:
@[Always] Grading feedback: Grade the recorded setup evidence and the complete vector-to-motion reasoning chain. BusyBee scoring: Award points only in 0.5-point increments, including whole points, from 0 to the question maximum. Select a rubric-supported allowed score; never report hundredths such as 2.85/3. Do not average or percentage-scale rubric criteria into an off-grid score. A binary completion rubric still permits only 0 or full credit. Allowed scores for this question: 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3.
a. Full credit: States a clear claim, cites the successful Challenge 3 charge arrangement, explains that individual fields add to a position-dependent net field, and connects net field to force, acceleration, and the changing velocity direction. Partial credit: Gives a reasonable design and mentions combined fields but omits specific evidence or one part of the reasoning chain. No credit: Claims fixed charges produce one unchanging force everywhere or provides no usable evidence.
